title: Python: a lazy class-body read (alias value, or an alias type parameter's bound, constraint or default) of a name the class body binds anywhere never resolves through an enclosing scope, a star import or a builtin; it refuses (DEC-303 (a76), folds N1a and N1b)
description: Wrong claims on dev (was on the hold list until started). WIDENED under DEC-303 (a76) (relayed by the leader 2026-11-27; supersedes this task's first scope). One rule: a LAZY class-body read, meaning an alias value or an alias type parameter's bound, constraint or default, of a name the class body binds ANYWHERE never resolves through an enclosing scope, a star import or a builtin. It REFUSES. Removal-only per (a73) item 2: it does NOT resolve to the class binding (m.len, m.f) because that would create edges. A lazy read runs after the class body, so it sees the class's FINAL binding; dev claims otherwise on these measured inputs (origin/dev 4e186bfb, identical on the GCLI-144 head; CPython 3.15.2 for the runtime answers). (1) the alias BOUND: class C with def run; x = C() at module level or in def outer(); class Outer: type A[T: x.run()] = int; from m import X as x: dev edges [C, C.run] (calls 2), runtime the bound reads m.X; the same for the constraint tuple type A[T: (x.run(), int)] = int. (2) N1a: m.py def len(o): pass; app.py class Outer: type A = len([]); from m import len: dev bins external 1, no edge (claims the BUILTIN len), runtime Outer.A.__value__ is m.len. (3) N1b: s.py def f(): pass; m.py def f(): pass; app.py from s import *; class Outer: type A = f(); from m import f: dev gives the edge app.py:3:14 to s.py:f, runtime m.f. Twins on dev: def f[T: x.run()](self) and class K[T: x.run()] in a class body record only x = C() (bounds of a def or class are not walked: GCLI-145, ordinary). Module-level type A[T: x.run()] = int with a single module x = C() gives C.run, correct there. MECHANISM (GCLI-144's marker, Scope.lazyAlias, already exists): walk an alias's type parameter bound, constraint and default in its lazy scope; and in lookupBindings a lazy read where Rule 38 dropped the class binding refuses even when nothing is bound further out, so the lookup must not return null (unbound, builtin, star) for it: that is the 'lazyDiffers && bindings.length > 0' condition pinned by GCLI-147, whose N1a and N1b fixtures this task turns from 'unchanged from dev' into REFUSED. PROOF: fixtures for the bound and constraint forms plus N1a and N1b, each red on dev and green after; a mutant per path, run red; the subset check, every head edge a dev edge and no new builtin or star claim, over the five pins, the fixtures and the 450-source corpus (add bound, constraint, default and builtin or star sources). Two review rounds (DEC-161). ORDER: after #225 and GCLI-147, before GCLI-140 (the (a25) attribute-write rule); the (a36) item 8 pre-registration, GCLI-143, waits. STARTED by the leader's go (DEC-303 (a76)); the hold label is removed while it is In Progress. Two review rounds under DEC-161.

implementationNotes: SCHEDULING (opum-doc, DEC-303 (a74) item 3, relayed by the leader 2026-11-27): the alias-bound wrong edge (the bound form type A[T: x.run()] and the constraint-tuple form type A[T: (x.run(), int)]) joins the (a49) item 7 hold list as a wrong-edge fix. Order: right after GCLI-144 and before GCLI-140 (the (a25) attribute-write rule); the (a36) item 8 pre-registration, GCLI-143, waits for it. It stays hold until the leader starts it. Two review rounds (DEC-161). Removal-only is proved by the same subset check as GCLI-144: every head edge is also a dev edge over the five pins, the fixtures and a differential corpus; any created edge or bin gain comes to opum-doc before the PR. GCLI-145 keeps the def and class bounds as an ordinary follow-up, not a hold.

Built (DEC-303 (a76)). Two changes in src/python/calls.ts: (1) lookupBindings: a lazy read whose class bindings Rule 38 ALL dropped, with nothing further out, returns a flagged empty result (lazyEmpty) instead of null, so the unbound path no longer claims a builtin or a star-supplied name; (2) a class-body alias's left side (its type parameters, bound and constraint) is walked in the lazy scope. The PEP 696 default cannot be exercised as a call site (parse error, calls under an error node dropped): no coverage claimed. All 14 lookupBindings consumers already refuse a flagged result (checked, none changed). Fixtures: 10 in describe GCLI-146 plus N1a and N1b updated to REFUSED (nameNotBound 1, no edge) in GCLI-147's block; 4 red on origin/dev bc74515 (N1a, N1b, bound, constraint). Mutants per path, run red: lazyEmpty return dropped 2, lazyEmpty never set 2, left side not lazy 2. Differential dev vs head over 734 sources (the 450 corpus plus bound, constraint, def and class bound, value, builtin and star sources): 0 head-only edges, 22 removed, 0 bin gains, all 28 changed sources in the new groups. Five-pin cmp IDENTICAL. bun test 1220 pass.

CORRECTION (measured, DEC-303 (a76) guard fixture): the earlier note and the PR text said a PEP 696 default cannot be exercised as a call site because calls under the error node are dropped. That is wrong for this grammar: for type A[T = x.run()] = int the parser makes an ERROR node of T only, and x.run() is a normal call under a sibling type node of the type_parameter, so it IS walked and recorded (calls 2, dropped 0). origin/dev: an eager read, the edge C.run (wrong, with a later class-body import of x); the head: refused (receiver 1, no edge), because the alias left side is walked in the lazy scope. The guard fixture asserts that and is red on dev; if a grammar upgrade changes how a default parses, a red there goes to opum-doc. Differential widened to 774 sources (adds default and bound-and-default forms): 0 head-only edges, 50 removed, 0 bin gains. Mutant left side not lazy: 3 red. bun test 1221.

Round 1 (Opus, head a25c6fe5) BLOCK, fixed locally: the left side of a GENERIC class-body alias was walked in the type-parameter scope, so a comprehension target inside a bound, constraint or default landed on that scope, not on the class as on dev (the GCLI-144 bindsInto precedent). Confirmed by running (a25c6fe5 against origin/dev): A, a bound binding len, gave a new builtin claim (external 1; dev nameNotBound 1); B, a bound binding helper, gave a new edge Outer.helper (dev receiver); C, a bound binding g, gave a new edge to module g (dev none); the constraint, set, dict and generator forms the same; the default form is identical on dev and head. Fix: the left side of a class-body alias is walked in a child scope of the alias scope that records binders on the class (leftScope.bindsInto), so a generic alias keeps its type parameter names on the type-parameter scope. Fixtures: 15 in describe 'binders inside a generic alias's bound stay on the class body' (A, B, C and the constraint, set, dict and generator forms, a default, twins, a function-level alias, a module-level alias unchanged, the eager twin len): 11 red on a25c6fe5, green after. Mutants run red: lazyEmpty unconditional 1 (the eager twin), left side walked for any type scope 1 (the module-level alias), leftScope.bindsInto removed 11, leftScope dropped 11, plus the earlier three. Differential over 954 sources (adds binders in bound, constraint and default across class body, nested class, def, module and function level aliases): head 0 head-only edges, 50 removed, 0 bin gains; a25c6fe5 on the same corpus: 54 head-only edges and 72 bin gains (positive control). Five-pin cmp IDENTICAL. Records: describe header and calls.ts comment fixed (default covered), the hold label and the Not started text removed while In Progress. bun test 1237.

CORRECTION OF MECHANISM (round 2, DEC-303 (a77)): the earlier CORRECTION note said a PEP 696 default is refused because the alias left side is walked in the lazy scope. Measured at 3d9caead: it is refused by the SUPERSET rule instead. typeParameterNames counts every identifier under a parse error in a type-parameter list as a type-parameter name, so in type A[T = x.run()] = int the names x, run (and f in type A[T = f()] = int) are type parameters of the alias's scope and each call refuses, with or without a later class-body binding. origin/dev gave C.run and the edge to f there; the head refuses both (class-body aliases only; a module-level or function-level default is unchanged). Removal-only, accepted over-refusal (DEC-303 (a77) item 1); restoring the edges is GCLI-148 (ordinary). A bound seeing the alias's own type parameters (T: T() with a module def T, [U, T: U()], [len, T: len([])]) is a measured removal, accepted (item 2). CORPUS COUNT: the final differential is 1394 constructed sources (the 450-source corpus, alias bounds, constraints, defaults, def and class bounds, alias values, builtin and star reads, and binders in every lazy position); the 734 and 774 in the earlier notes were intermediate runs and 954 was the corpus before the value-position sources. The fixtures pinning these cases are in the test-and-records PR (test/python-hops.test.ts).
finalSummary: Landed as opum-ai/glyph-cli#228 (squash 18b68a7941be7bdf97b2938f2ead2635f2170f99): DEC-303 (a76)/(a77), removal-only. A lazy class-body read (alias value, alias type parameter bound, constraint or default) of a name the class body binds refuses and never resolves through an enclosing scope, a star import or a builtin (N1a and N1b folded in); binders inside a bound stay on the class as on dev. Opus round 1 BLOCK (binders in a generic alias's bound, fixed), round 2 APPROVE-WITH-NOTES. Differential over 1394 sources: 0 head-only edges, 50 removed, 0 bin gains; five-pin cmp identical. Accepted over-refusal: calls in a class-body alias default (superset rule), GCLI-148.
